comments:
The author of an early Tibetan indigenous commentary on the Nyāyabindu (ID: 7165), whose first chapter is preserved in Tangut translation. 
The author's name appears only in Tangut in the colophon as "Źjɨr ɣwie." Because the first word, źjɨr, means "insight" and the second, "ɣwie," means "victory," the name can possibly be reconstructed as Shes rab rgyal ba. 
Many features of the commentary, such as the hermeneutic tools utilized and the persons cited in there, indicate the author was part of the intellectual tradition stemming from rNgog Blo ldan shes rab (ID:3786). 
The author quotes from early followers of rNgog Lo, such as Khyung Rin chen grags (ID:3809). However, in the extant part of the commentary, we do not see him quoting from Phya pa (ID:3831) or anyone after him. This suggests he was likely a contemporary of Phya pa. 
Also, a certain "Sher rgyal" documented in the Red Annals fits with Źjɨr ɣwie's intellectual and biographical profiles - see (ID:7975). Hence, they could be the same person. 

 For details, see [3HXACZSD]: 208–216.
